record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.original_question: Clarify the exact mathematical relationship between CTCS(∞), the exchangeable-partition limit of the critical beta-splitting model, and the beta(2,1) coalescent, beyond the paper's observed coincidences involving the same subordinator and parallel asymptotics for collision or hop-count statistics.

evidence.quote: There is in fact another closely related continuous model, the beta(2, 1) coalescent [66].
Open Problem 19 Elucidate the precise connections between CTCS(∞) and the beta(2, 1) coalescent.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup.

(a) Critical beta-splitting and CTCS(∞). For each integer n ≥ 2, define a random binary tree on n labeled leaves by the following recursive splitting rule: a clade containing m ≥ 2 leaves is partitioned into two sub-clades of sizes i and m − i with probability
  q(m, i) = (1/Z_m) · 1/(i(m − i)),  1 ≤ i ≤ m − 1,
where Z_m = ∑_{i=1}^{m−1} 1/(i(m − i)). Iterating until all clades are singletons yields the discrete critical beta-splitting tree. Endow each internal node v that splits a clade of size m with a real-valued "time" coordinate such that times along any root-to-leaf path are decreasing, with edge lengths chosen according to the natural continuous-time embedding (the clade of size m holds for an independent waiting time before splitting). Call the resulting random metric tree on n leaves CTCS(n). The family (CTCS(n))_{n≥2} is consistent under the operation "delete a uniformly chosen leaf and contract the resulting degree-2 vertex," and admits a projective limit CTCS(∞), an exchangeable random structure encoding the partitions of N obtained by removing all edges at times above a given threshold.

(b) The beta(2, 1) coalescent. Let Λ be the probability measure on [0, 1] with density f(x) = 2(1 − x) (the Beta(1, 2) density). The Λ-coalescent associated to Λ, in the case Λ = Beta(2, 1) (i.e. f(x) = 2(1 − x)), is the exchangeable coalescent process Π(t) on partitions of N whose rate of merging any specified k of the b current blocks into one is
  λ_{b,k} = ∫_0^1 x^{k−2}(1 − x)^{b−k} Λ(dx),  2 ≤ k ≤ b.
This coalescent comes-down-from-infinity and is associated with a stable-type subordinator.

Both CTCS(∞) and the beta(2, 1) coalescent are known to share the same underlying subordinator and to produce matching asymptotics for several functionals (e.g. collision counts and hop counts).

Problem. Determine the precise mathematical relationship between CTCS(∞) and the beta(2, 1) coalescent. Specifically, exhibit an explicit coupling, time-change, or functional transformation that maps one exchangeable structure to the other (or prove that no such coupling exists), and identify which joint distributional features of the two processes coincide and which differ.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the literature on the critical beta-splitting random tree. Subsequent work on the critical beta-splitting model (e.g., the 2024 "Critical beta-splitting, via contraction" paper) does not announce an elucidation of the precise CTCS(∞)–beta(2,1)-coalescent connection, so the problem appears to remain open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems concerning CTCS(∞), including elucidating connections with the beta(2,1) coalescent.
status_evidence.claim: The connection is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Critical beta-splitting, via contraction
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on CTCS(n) and contraction methods; does not announce a resolution of the CTCS(∞)/beta(2,1)-coalescent comparison.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution claimed in subsequent work.
